sources.entry: Fenestra - Windows 11 desktop for macOS with a taskbar, Start menu, Snap Layouts, Alt+Tab and clipboard history. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/PRMotorWorks/Fenestra) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Fenestra is a free, native macOS app that replaces the Dock and menu bar with a Windows 11-style desktop, including a taskbar, Start menu, Snap Layouts, Alt+Tab and clipboard history.
summary.what_it_does: Fenestra hides the Dock and menu bar and shows a Windows 11-style taskbar with pinned and open apps, live window previews, and a jump list. It provides a Start menu with pinned apps, recent files, an app list, and search, opened by tapping Command. A Quick Settings panel offers Wi-Fi and Bluetooth lists, volume and brightness sliders, and configurable tiles. Every window gets minimize, maximize and close buttons, and Snap Layouts or edge dragging place windows into halves, thirds or quarters. Option+Tab switches windows, Control+Option+V opens clipboard history for text, links, images and files, and a taskbar appears on each connected display. Each change Fenestra makes to macOS has its own switch, and quitting restores the original setup.
use_cases: make a Mac feel like Windows 11
snap and tile windows on macOS
Alt+Tab style window switching on macOS
replace the Dock with a taskbar
keep Windows shortcuts when switching to a Mac
how_to_run: Download Fenestra.dmg and drag Fenestra to Applications
Open Fenestra; approve it in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway (one time)
Turn on Accessibility (required) and Screen & System Audio Recording (for window previews)
To build from source: open the project in Xcode (see DEVELOPMENT.md)
notable: Restores Dock and menu bar on quit, and at next login if the app was dragged to Trash
Makes no network connections: no analytics, accounts or update checks, per the README
Every macOS change has its own toggle in Taskbar settings
Quick snap lets a fling toward an edge land the window there
Idles at 0% CPU and uses about 60 MB of memory, per the README
caveats: Not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS shows a warning on first launch and needs manual approval
Needs Accessibility permission, and Screen Recording for window previews
